The novel "Sense and Sensibility" by Jane Austen begins with the introduction of the Dashwood family, who have lived in Sussex at Norland Park for generations. The late owner of the estate, Mr. Norland, had invited his nephew, Mr. Henry Dashwood, and his family to live with him after the death of his sister, who had been his housekeeper. Mr. Norland grew fond of his nephew's family, particularly his three daughters, and was comforted by their presence.

However, when Mr. Norland dies, his will is read, and it is revealed that he has left the majority of his estate to his great-nephew, a child of four years old, instead of his nephew. This leaves Mr. Dashwood with only £7,000, which is insufficient to support his wife and three daughters. The will also provides for the great-nephew's education and well-being, but ties up the majority of the estate, leaving Mr. Dashwood without the means to provide for his own family.

Mr. Dashwood's disappointment is severe, but he tries to remain cheerful and hopes to live for many years and accumulate a substantial sum of money from his existing estate. However, he dies just a year after his uncle's death, leaving his widow and daughters with only £10,000, including a legacy of £1,000 each for his three daughters.

The novel then introduces Mr. John Dashwood, Mr. Dashwood's son, who is summoned to his father's bedside. The dying Mr. Dashwood urges Mr. John to take care of his mother and sisters, but it is unclear whether Mr. John will fulfill this responsibility.
